rules.title: Release every allocation on every path
rules.what: Each malloc/calloc/realloc has an identified free on every path, error paths included; reuse buffers in loops instead of reallocating; run a sanitizer or leak check on changed code.
rules.why: A leak holds memory until the process ends; reallocating in a loop spends CPU in the allocator for no gain.
rules.how: Single exit with cleanup labels, ownership documented at each public boundary; -fsanitize=address,leak or valgrind in CI.

patterns.note: Allocation inside a loop body; candidate for buffer reuse.

verify.how: ASan/LSan or valgrind run on the changed code reports no leak.

rules.title: Hoist strlen, avoid repeated strcat
rules.what: Compute string lengths once before loops and keep an end pointer instead of repeated strcat().
rules.why: strlen in a loop condition and strcat both rescan the string from the start: quadratic work invisible on reading.
rules.how: size_t n = strlen(s); before the loop; memcpy at a tracked offset; snprintf with a running length.

patterns.note: strcat rescans the destination; quadratic in a loop.

verify.how: No strlen in loop conditions; no strcat in loops.

rules.title: Buffered I/O, blocking waits
rules.what: Use buffered block I/O (fread/fwrite) instead of byte-by-byte calls, and block on poll/epoll/select or a condition variable instead of busy waiting.
rules.why: One system call per byte multiplies kernel transitions; a spin or short-sleep loop keeps a core busy and prevents low-power states.
rules.how: fread into a buffer; setvbuf for streams; poll()/epoll_wait() or pthread_cond_wait for readiness.

verify.how: No per-byte I/O loop on large data; no busy wait.

rules.title: Standard optimisation, warnings kept
rules.what: Build production with standard supported optimisation (-O2), keep warnings and undefined-behaviour fixes, and benchmark aggressive flags before adopting them.
rules.why: Debug builds waste CPU at every run; aggressive flags can trade correctness for an unmeasured gain.
rules.how: -O2 -Wall -Wextra in release; -O3/-march or LTO only with a benchmark; compact structs (watch padding) on massively instantiated types.

verify.how: Release flags documented; any non-standard flag backed by a benchmark.
